## Overview

**In plain terms.** Did the children offered the intervention read more single words than those who were not — and how large, and how certain, is that difference? This model estimates the assigned-arm contrast among children with the required word-reading observations in the fitted analysis set. Randomisation created exchangeability in the original full randomised cohort, but conditioning on archive inclusion and observed analytic variables can break it. A causal reading of the fitted contrast therefore requires selection not to induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

LRPITT10 is the available-case modified ITT analysis for word reading (EWRSWR) (`ewrswr`). The estimand is the assigned-arm contrast in the post-score $W_{\text{post}}$ among children with the required word-reading observations, using the RCT phase only (time 1 $\rightarrow$ time 2).
This model supersedes LRP52.

The original paper reported Mplus ANCOVAs adjusted for the corresponding t1 score, t1 age and gender, with full-information maximum likelihood for the small amount of missing data within its 54-child analysed cohort (28 intervention, 26 waiting control). That does not make the paper a full-57 analysis: three randomised children were lost to follow-up. The Bayesian model of record below uses the 53 children with observed t1 and t2 word-reading scores and adjusts for t1 word reading and age as precision terms. Its mandatory secondary sensitivity therefore first refits those same 53 outcomes using the screening word-reading and screening-age measures available for all 57 children, with an intercept prior anchored only to the pre-randomisation screening distribution. It then separates common-profile all-57 MAR standardisation from factual completion of the 29 and 28 randomised arms under explicit no-benefit and delta assumptions.

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked causal DAG, $G$ is a randomised root, so the offer contrast in the original full randomised cohort requires no baseline-covariate adjustment. This fit instead conditions on archive inclusion and observed word-reading variables; a causal reading of $\tau$ in the fitted sample requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes, and extending it to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity. The own baseline $\gamma_{\text{own}}$ and linear age $\gamma_A$ are **precision terms only** — they may sharpen $\tau$ but do not identify effects after selection — and no cross-baseline conditioning is used. Attendance or sessions are never conditioned on (a DAG collider). **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the intervention arm has the higher modelled outcome.

## Model

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \text{logit}_*(W_{\mathrm{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i},
$$

with Beta-Binomial likelihood $W_{\text{post},i} \sim \text{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu_i\kappa, (1-\mu_i)\kappa)$,
$\mu_i = \sigma(\eta_i)$, $N = 79$. Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
HSGPs on age and own baseline are off by default (the 2026-04-18 sensitivity
verdict).

Word reading is heavily floored at *baseline* (t1, ~40% at zero) but not at the
post-score (t2), so the floor rule (which gates on the t2 post-score) does not
trip and the graded own-baseline specification is retained; the baseline floor
simply makes $\gamma_{\text{own}}$ less informative.
